name: STAR Geodesy — polar stereographic and UPS
summary: Polar stereographic projection at either pole with any parallel of true scale, forward, inverse and scale factor, and the UPS grid; within 7e-8 m of PROJ and 5e-9 m of PyGeodesy on 600 cases; reproduces Snyder's published example and refuses out-of-range input.
reference: Snyder, Map Projections - A Working Manual (USGS PP 1395), p. 314: International ellipsoid, south polar aspect, true scale 71 S, central meridian 100 W, point 75 S 150 E: x = -1540033.6 m, y = -560526.4 m
reference_observed: (-1540033.611, -560526.394): within 0.011 m of the printed values (printed to 0.1 m)

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: degrees and metres; pole letter; axes orientation at each pole stated; false origins of UPS stated
review.G-06: no external data; cross-check corpus generated with a fixed seed
review.G-08: pure functions, standard library only, no IO
review.G-13: ValueError for every invalid input; Newton iteration capped at 10 steps; the pole handled as an exact case
